rationale: This is a mechanical crossing of two already-tested levers (triple gate × IND_RANK) rather than a new mechanism, and the stated motivation misreads the archive — industry-relative ranking *lowered* both the alpha (6.2%→4.6%) and the ls_talpha (4.48→4.00), so there is no demonstrated "lift" to combine.

The diagnosis (large multiplicative alpha with a dead FMB slope suggests fat-tailed z-score weighting) is coherent and the fix — recasting the internal-minus-acquired leg into the bounded conjunctive form that has worked elsewhere — is a substantive, sign-consistent test rather than a cosmetic reparameterization.

The expression is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis because R&D expense is a cash operating outflow already deducted inside oancf, so SUB(oancf, xrd) double-subtracts research spending rather than measuring "cash left after paying for R&D," and the remaining gate is close to the well-known cash-based operating profitability anomaly.

The construction is orientation-consistent with the negative expected sign and plausibly repairs the family's weak short leg, but the resulting short portfolio (intangible-heavy, unprofitable pre-R&D, accrual-supported) is close to a generic junk/distress screen, so a significant result may add little beyond the profitability and accrual anomalies already known.
This is a pure lookback-window tweak (MA 3 → MA 5) of ConjunctiveIntangibleEarningsQuality with no new economic content, exactly the kind of cosmetic variant the objective asks to avoid.

Swapping the pre-R&D ROA gate for a revenue-side margin gate is a genuine test of whether the triple-gate gain comes from profitability information generally or from the ib-sharing bottom-line channel, though unadjusted gross margin is strongly industry-determined and an IND_RANK version would be the cleaner comparison.
